hero.title: Live and Work in Bali Hassle-Free
hero.subtitle: Embrace the excitement of effortless journeying and remote work in Bali, the tropical paradise of the archipelago.

about.text: Digital Nomad Indonesia aims to empower remote workers in Indonesia through sustainable practices, cultural exchange, community engagement, and providing resources and networking opportunities.

items.title: Gorgeous Landscapes, Picture-Perfect Beaches
items.text: Explore verdant rice paddies that stretch on forever, go on an adventure through dense jungle, or even climb a volcano. Venture further into the ocean and engage in water sports like scuba diving or snorkeling.

items.title: Distinct Art Forms and Vibrant Society
items.text: You can feel the positive energy and enthusiasm of the Balinese people in nearly every facet of their distinctive culture — the culture that draws artists and those interested in yoga and mindfulness from all over the globe.

items.title: A Proven Tourist Attraction
items.text: Bali is convenient whether you're just passing through or want to make it a permanent home and live the nomadic life. The built-up districts provide excellent places to work or stay.

cost.title: Cost of Living
cost.text: The relatively low cost of living is yet another wonderful aspect of Bali. If you're strapped for cash, you can get dinner for a dollar and a hostel bed for five. A two-bedroom villa can be yours for as little as $500 per month on a longer stay — and on a moderate budget, $1,000 a month should be plenty.

visa.title: Visa Options for Digital Nomads in Bali
visa.subtitle: Make sure you have all the documentation in place before leaving for your workation in Bali.

items.title: Remote Worker Visa
items.text: Valid for a maximum of one year with multiple entries, for remote workers employed by companies located outside Indonesia.

items.title: Electronic Visa on Arrival
items.text: A single-entry visa valid for 30 days including the day of arrival. It can be extended once for another 30 days.

items.title: Multiple Entry Visas
items.text: A multi-entry visa valid for 1, 2, or 5 years, allowing stays of up to 60 days, extendable twice for 60 days each without leaving the country.

destinations.title: Top Destinations for Digital Nomads in Bali

items.name: Canggu
items.text: A small town and 8km coastal stretch just north of Seminyak, regarded as a top surfing destination since the 1970s. With an abundance of co-working and co-living spaces and laid-back surfer rhythms, many call it the perfect destination for a digital nomad.

items.name: Ubud
items.text: The best place if you want somewhere more peaceful. Known for its chill vibe, you can get a lot of work done in peace and quiet, then rest with a walk in the woods or one of the many yoga classes and retreats in the area.

items.q: What are Indonesia visas for business?
items.a: There are two types of Indonesia Business Visa: Multiple Entry and Single Entry. The Single Entry Business Visa is valid for 60 days and is extendable up to 3 times, while the Multiple Entry Business Visa is valid for 12 months.

items.q: How do I expand my business in Indonesia?
items.a: The most common route for foreigners is setting up a PT PMA (foreign-owned limited liability company). Our legal team handles company registration, licensing, and compliance end to end.

items.q: How many types of tax are there in Indonesia?
items.a: The main taxes are corporate income tax, personal income tax, and Value Added Tax (VAT/PPN), along with withholding taxes. We help you obtain an NPWP and stay compliant.

faqPage.tagline: Answers to the questions we hear most about visas, permits and doing business in Indonesia.

items.q: What are Indonesia visas for business?
items.a: There are two types of Indonesia Business Visa: Multiple Entry and Single Entry. The Single Entry Business Visa is valid for 60 days and is extendable up to 3 times, while the Multiple Entry Business Visa is valid for 12 months.

items.q: How do I expand my business in Indonesia?
items.a: The most common route for foreigners is setting up a PT PMA (foreign-owned limited liability company). Our legal team handles company registration, licensing and compliance end to end.

items.q: How many types of tax are there in Indonesia?
items.a: The main taxes are corporate income tax, personal income tax, and Value Added Tax (VAT/PPN), along with withholding taxes. We help you obtain an NPWP and stay compliant.

items.q: Which visa is best for digital nomads?
items.a: The Remote Worker (Digital Nomad) Visa suits those employed by a company outside Indonesia, while the B211 single-entry visa is popular for longer holidays and remote stays. We'll recommend the best fit for your situation.

items.q: Can I extend my Visa on Arrival?
items.a: Yes. A Visa on Arrival can be extended once for an additional 30 days without leaving the country, and we manage the entire process for you.

items.q: Do you help with KITAS and KITAP?
items.a: Yes. We process Investor, Working, Family and Retirement KITAS, and can guide you toward a longer-term KITAP where eligible.

items.q: How long does the process take?
items.a: Timelines vary by visa type, but we always give you a realistic estimate up front and keep you updated at every stage.

items.q: Do you offer services outside Bali?
items.a: Yes. While we're based in Canggu, we assist clients across Indonesia with visas, legal setup and relocation.
